english: how do you say it in Latin?
also: how do you say … in Latin?
how would you say that in Latin?

terms.gloss: how is this said in Latin?
terms.grammar: Latīnē, adverb, “in Latin”; dīcitur, present passive of dīcō
evidence: Sen. Ep. 58.6: Quid enim fīet, mī Lūcīlī? quōmodo dīcētur (of a Greek philosophical word)
Cic. ND 1.8: quae ā Graecīs accēpissent, Latīnē dīcī posse diffīderent
terms.comment: Our sentence, made of Seneca’s question about a Greek word for which he wants a Latin one, quōmodo dīcētur …?, and Cicero’s Latīnē dīcere, “say in Latin”. We have found no classical instance of the whole question: the authors more often give the answer, Graecē haec vocātur …, eadem Latīnē … (Plaut. Merc. 9–10). Put the word asked about in place of hoc (see the examples). For the name of a thing in front of you, see “name”.

terms.gloss: how is … to be said? (asking for the Latin of a foreign word)
evidence: Sen. Ep. 58.6: quōmodo dīcētur, followed by the Greek word
terms.comment: Seneca’s own question, in a letter about the poverty of Latin beside Greek; the future asks what one is to say.

evidence: Cic. ND 1.8: Latīnē dīcī posse diffīderent
Cic. Opt. Gen. 23: Aeschinem ipsum Latīnē dīcentem audiāmus
Traupman 248: Latīnē loquī, to speak (correct) Latin

terms.gloss: put into Latin, find the Latin for
evidence: Sen. Ep. 58.7: id nūllō modō Latīnē exprimere possim

terms.gloss: be called in Latin (the answer: “in Latin it’s …”)
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.142: tempus autem āctiōnis opportūnum Graecē … Latīnē appellātur occāsiō
Plaut. Merc. 9–10: Graecē haec vocātur Emporos Philēmonis, eadem Latīnē Mercātor

phrases.english: How do you say “fork” in Latin? — Furcilla.

phrases.latin: Graecē haec vocātur Emporos Philēmonis, eadem Latīnē Mercātor Maccī Titī.
phrases.english: In Greek this play is called Emporos, by Philemon; in Latin the same play is Mercator, by Titus Maccius.

phrases.latin: et quidem saepe quaerimus verbum Latīnum par Graecō et quod idem valeat
phrases.english: and indeed we often look for a Latin word to match a Greek one, with the same force
